pr_title: Bug fix for hyprctl --batch doesn't work with exec rules
pr_body:
#### Describe your PR, what does it fix/add?
Fixes #1820 by ignoring ';' inside brackets [ ]

#### Is there anything you want to mention? (unchecked code, possible bugs, found problems, breaking compatibility, etc.)

For some reason the only app that was problematic when testing using commands like this -> 
`hyprctl --batch 'dispatch exec [noanim;float;workspace 7 silent] appname; dispatch exec [noanim;float;workspace 6 silent] appname; dispatch exec appname;'` 
was Wezterm, it would spawn on whatever workspace, other than that everything else worked without issues

#### Is it ready for merging, or does it need work?
Yeah, I was testing it with different apps and different combinations of commands and as mentioned above only Wezterm was problematic

issue_context.title: hyprctl --batch doesn't work with exec rules
issue_context.body:
I'm trying to do something like this:
```bash
hyprctl --batch "\
dispatch exec [noanim;float;workspace name:$SELECTED silent] kitty;\
etc..."
```

The rules for exec in square brackets don't work because the semicolon is used as delimiter for the batch command as well.
comments:
Yes. I ran this command:
```console
❯ hyprctl --batch 'dispatch exec [workspace 10 silent;group] flatpak run org.mozilla.Thunderbird'
okunknown request
```

As you can see, it is interpreted as two commands due to the dumb split on ";", though I'm also not sure why the "exec" got an okay with invalid syntax

review_comments:
what about the last argument?
`cmda ; cmdb ; cmdc`
won't cmdc not be parsed? it doesn't have a `;` at the end that we can find.

That is why on line 1162 there is ternary to add virtual ';' for last command, without it last command would get ignored. From my testing everything from commands that end in no ';' or even with multiple ';' in case of miss input will just work.

So stuff like `cmda ; cmdb ; cmdc` or `cmda ; cmdb ; cmdc;;;;;;;` will return "ok" 3 times, ofc if the commands itself do have proper syntax
Let me know if this approach in general is ok for you for this bug fix. This is my first pull request ever so I kinda don't know the dynamics of this lol
